**Studio design coordination (Luis's lane): the UI of this PR measured against the kit, and the merge with the kit stack prepared.**

Read on the head `d527f385` merged over the kit stack's head (#254, `27f310f2`) at `ui/kit-with-con01` (`574766cd`): headless Chromium at 1280×800 and 390×844, `pointer: fine`. Captures and `measures.json` are in Luis's evaluation folder; the numbers below are from them. Nothing here blocks G3; the first two are the kind of thing `control-heights.spec` would name if the confirmations were open when it reads.

1. **The two confirmations use the legacy `.button`, off the controls' grid.** `WithdrawHere.tsx:181` and `EraseHere.tsx:127` render `className="button"`: measured 26 px tall, grey fill, square radius, beside «Keep it» as a `.text-button` (24). In the same context pane the kit's «Accept» is a `.pill` at 28. The kit's rule (CONTRIBUTING, `control-heights.spec`): every single-line press stands on 24, 28, 32 or 36. The kit has `Button` from `@sophia/ui` (`kind`, `size`) and `ConfirmButton` for a question asked in place (Stop on a goal uses it: a `warning`, a `confirm` word, a `keep` word). Suggest `ConfirmButton` for both, or `Button` with the destructive kind if one is added; the words stay.

2. **The press and its form name the act differently for a moderator.** `WithdrawHere.tsx:85` labels the press «Remove message» when the message is another's and «Withdraw message» when it is one's own; the form's group is labelled accordingly (`:166`), but the visible question reads «Withdraw this message? …» in both cases (measured text of the group). One word for one act, in the press, the group and the sentence.

3. **«Covers messages 1–9.» twice in the context pane.** The summary's coverage and the open questions' coverage are two lines with the same words, one under «This conversation», one under «1 open question»; read together they look like a repeat. Either one coverage line for the pane, or words that say what each covers («The questions cover 1–9.»).

4. **The withdraw press is an absolutely positioned span; in the kit it is a row item.** The kit's Conversations (#240) put Copy, Quote and Propose in one acts row (`.conv-acts`, 28 px presses on `--r-2`, hidden until hover/press) mounted in the message's turn. `WithdrawHere` renders `<span class="conv-withdraw">` with `position: absolute; right: 22px` to sit beside `.conv-propose`. In the merge I render `away.press` inside the row and add `.conv-acts .conv-withdraw { position: static }`; it lands as the fourth press (measured: four 28×28 presses, the row 130 px, at the turn's right edge at both widths). If #199 lands first, the kit's merge brings that; if the kit lands first, `WithdrawHere` can drop its own positioning.

5. **The saved-text notice did not render in the demo fixture** (`room.html?demo=1&conversations=1`: the reader has already written), so it is not measured here. Point me at a fixture state that shows it and I will measure it against the five sizes and the third ink.

**Merge preparation.** `ui/kit-with-con01` holds this PR merged over the kit stack's head with the conflicts resolved: `ConversationRows.tsx` (one import), `OpenConversation.tsx` (both `onQuote` and `withdraw` thread through the list; a withdrawn message, `text === null`, shows no acts; `MessageLead` + `MessageBy` + `useArrivalFocus` keep the two functions under the repository's 60 lines), `conversations.css` (the touch rules unioned), `ProjectShell.tsx` (the kit's shell with this PR's `CONVERSATIONS` flag and `useProjectMembership(…, snapshot.dataUpdatedAt)`), and the generated contracts regenerated from A15 and A16 together (`contracts:check` clean). Lint and typecheck clean; locally 135 of 136 Conversations and kit specs green, the one left being `conversations-removal @phone` «an erasure's late reply…», which passes one run in two here (timing). Whichever lands second can take these resolutions.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep dismissed asks out of the quick actions**

When the suggested ask is one of the three quick asks, pressing Escape records it in `putAway` and sets `suggestion` to null, but this call then immediately adds the same words back to the quick-action row because `quickAsks` receives neither the dismissed words nor the pre-dismissal suggestion. For example, with one open question and no pending proposal, dismissing “What’s still open?” makes an identical button appear below the field, so the ask was not actually put away for the lifetime of the conversation.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Base recency on six viewer messages**

The initial transcript request contains only one page—the fixture contract makes that the newest six messages total—and earlier pages are loaded only when the user presses “Earlier messages.” Filtering that loaded slice for the current actor can therefore yield fewer than the intended six viewer messages; in an alternating conversation it sees only three, so an ask made four viewer turns ago is proposed again until older history happens to be opened. The recency input needs enough viewer-authored history rather than only the currently loaded page set.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make the suggestion reason keyboard-accessible**

For keyboard-only and screen-reader users, focusing the composer cannot expose `why`: the wrapper is not focusable, `Tip` is `aria-hidden`, and the `aria-describedby` text includes only the suggested words and key actions. This makes the newly added rationale pointer-only; include `why` in the described text or otherwise associate it with a focusable control, as required by the Studio UI tip convention.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Advance only after the answer is recorded**

When the answer API returns `conflict`, `denied`, `expired`, or `unknown`, this wrapper has already marked the decision as answered and displayed/focused the next-up line. The still-unanswered decision is therefore omitted and the viewer can be directed to another task—or told nothing else waits—while the decision's own status says nothing was chosen; update the progression from the returned disposition, retaining the current decision for every result except `recorded`.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include pending requests on non-waiting tasks**

A task can have a pending request for the viewer while its lifecycle is `planned`, `queued`, `unknown`, or otherwise not rendered with the `waiting` mark; `startsWhen`, `forViewer`, and `forYou` already treat such `row.waits` entries as work requiring that viewer. Requiring `status.mark === 'waiting'` therefore drops those tasks from Next up, which can incorrectly advance to a review or say nothing else waits. Select rows by a pending wait whose `respondent_id` is the viewer, as the existing viewer-attention predicates do.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Suppress the question shortcut while a send is held**

When a question is sent with Ask Sophia off and the request remains pending, `held` here is false because the caller passes `write.unknown`, which excludes `props.held.sending`. The question hint therefore remains visible and Tab changes the persisted Ask Sophia state even though the already-issued request has `askSophia: false`; the UI then says “Sophia will answer” for a message that did not ask her. Treat any pending `props.held`/busy state as held before offering this shortcut.

When a keyboard user activates this button, `openOne` closes the form and unmounts the focused element, but this path never focuses the opened thread as the `arrived` path does. On a phone, the screen therefore switches to the conversation with focus left on `document.body`, so the next Tab starts from page order and a screen reader receives no focused destination. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude sessions already under way from preparation asks**

When a session has started but not ended, the project API still returns it as `nextSession` (`packages/persistence/src/project-list.ts:33-43`), and `soon()` treats its negative minute count as eligible. This selection therefore shows “Help me get ready…” with “Because it started” throughout the session; it also sorts that session ahead of another one that is genuinely about to start.
